title: Spaghetti & Smashed Meatballs (Justin cut)
imageCredit: Reference stock photo by Diego Ramirez on Unsplash (Unsplash License)
creator: Stealth Health Life
summary: Big-batch Stealth Health Life spaghetti with smashed meatballs — oven-browned XL beef meatballs smashed crispy, simmered into a garlic-tomato bone-broth sauce with the pasta cooked right in. Justin cut keeps it mild (light/optional black pepper, no chili flakes), keeps the lean high-protein beef load, and calls out protein-pasta / half-and-half / zoodle paths plus 13–15 serving stretches for lower cal. Meal-prep friendly — Justin loves pasta.
whyItFits: Already high protein (~50g/serving at 10 portions) from 93% lean beef + Parm + bone broth
Mild Italian — no red pepper flakes; black pepper light or optional
Huge batch → meal prep for the week
Easy lower-carb / lower-cal swaps without losing the smashed-meatball vibe

items: ½–1 tsp black pepper (light / optional — mild cut; original uses 1 tsp)
900g (32 oz) spaghetti — or Justin lower-carb path (see Substitutions)

steps: Mix meatball ingredients; form ~14 XL meatballs on a sheet pan.
Sauce: 1 Tbsp oil, brown onions; add 1 Tbsp oil + garlic + tomato paste 3–4 min; add crushed tomatoes, bone broth, and water; simmer.
Bake meatballs 400°F 10 min, broil high ~7 min; pour pan juices into the sauce; smash flat; broil ~7 min more until crispy edges.
Add spaghetti to the simmering sauce (break in half if needed); salt + Italian seasoning; simmer uncovered, stirring often, 20–30 min until tender.
Add smashed meatballs; mix so beef integrates; simmer to thickness; finish with fresh basil.
Divide into servings (10 / 13 / 15 — see macros); top with Parm.
substitutions: Mild / no spice: keep black pepper light or omit; no red pepper flakes. Italian seasoning + garlic + Parm + San Marzano carry the flavor.

High protein (already strong): keep 93% lean beef. Optional: blend half beef + half lean ground chicken/turkey for a lighter flavor while holding protein — or bump beef slightly if stretching to 15 servings and want ~40g+ protein each.

Lower carb: swap all or part of the 900g spaghetti for protein spaghetti (Barilla Protein+, chickpea, etc.), half regular + half protein pasta, or cook classic pasta for some portions and use zoodles for others. Original is ~80g carbs/serving at 10 servings — protein pasta / zoodles cut that hard.
Lower cal: divide the same batch into 13 or 15 servings (caption alternate sizes) instead of 10.
Meal prep: cool, portion into containers, refrigerate 3–4 days or freeze. Reheat with a splash of bone broth or water so sauce stays loose.
Sweeteners: not needed — savory tomato dish. Save stevia / monk fruit / 0-sugar syrup for BBQ-honey / teriyaki nights.
notes: Source: Stealth Health Life Facebook reel — https://www.facebook.com/reel/2129879777597249/
Caption gives exact gram weights + 10-serving macros and suggests stretching servings for lower cal.
Smashed + broiled edges are the texture move — don’t skip the second broil.
Pasta cooks in the sauce (one-pot style); stir often so it doesn’t stick.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Stealth Health Life caption macros stretched to 13 servings (~512 cal / 38g protein). Original @ 10 servings: 665/50/80/15. Protein-pasta swaps lower carbs. Not lab-tested.

title: Mild Chicken Teriyaki Bowls
imageCredit: Reference stock photo by cole yap on Pexels (Pexels License)
creator: Chef's Cookbook (sample)
summary: SAMPLE — Low-sugar teriyaki chicken bowls sweetened with monk fruit / 0-sugar syrup. Mild, high-protein, Asian-inspired comfort over cauliflower rice or a small scoop of jasmine.

items: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast, cubed
1/3 cup low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos
2 tbsp 0-sugar simple syrup (or 1–2 tsp monk fruit extract to taste)
Optional: 1 tbsp sugar-free ketchup for body
3 cups cauliflower rice (or 1.5 cups cooked jasmine for half-and-half)

steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Sear in oil over medium-high until cooked through (165°F). Set aside.
In the same pan, whisk soy sauce, 0-sugar syrup (or monk fruit), vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger. Simmer 1–2 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch slurry; cook until glossy and slightly thick. Taste — add more monk fruit if you want sweeter, never chili.
Return chicken to the pan and coat in sauce.
Build bowls: cauliflower rice, broccoli, edamame, teriyaki chicken. Finish with sesame and green onion.
substitutions: Sweeteners: stevia, monk fruit extract, or 0-sugar syrup — start low and adjust.
Lower carb: full cauliflower rice; skip jasmine.
Extra protein: add edamame or a soft-boiled egg.
No spice: skip chili crisp / sriracha entirely — ginger + garlic carry it.
notes: SAMPLE placeholder — invent your own ratios when you cook it.
Coconut aminos are naturally a bit sweeter and milder than soy.

nutritionPerServing.notes: SAMPLE estimate: 1.5 lb chicken, cauliflower rice base, light teriyaki with 0-sugar syrup. Not lab-tested.

title: Garlic Chicken Protein Noodles
imageCredit: Reference stock photo by Mohammad Fahim on Unsplash (Unsplash License)
creator: Chef's Cookbook (sample)
summary: SAMPLE — Garlicky stir-fried chicken over high-protein noodles. Mild, savory, and built for Justin’s no-spice / high-protein lane. One tried + rated sample so the dashboard has a rating point.
whyItFits: Protein noodles keep carbs in check
Tried & rated sample for dashboard charts

items: 8 oz protein spaghetti or high-protein Asian-style noodles
3 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce or coconut aminos
Splash of chicken broth if needed
2 cups baby spinach or bok choy

steps: Cook protein noodles per package until just al dente; drain and toss with a drop of oil.
Sear chicken in avocado oil until nearly done. Add garlic and green onion whites; cook 30–60 seconds until fragrant (don’t burn garlic).
Add mushrooms if using; cook until soft. Splash in soy, oyster sauce, sesame oil, pepper, and optional 0-sugar syrup.
Toss in noodles and spinach until wilted and coated. Loosen with broth if sticky.
Plate and top with green onion greens. No chili oil — keep it mild.
substitutions: Noodles: Barilla Protein+, edamame pasta, or shirataki for ultra-low carb.
Sweetener: skip or use a drop of monk fruit if the sauce tastes sharp.
Extra protein: add an egg scrambled into the pan at the end.
notes: SAMPLE — marked tried with a 4.5 rating for dashboard demo.
Justin notes (fictional sample): ‘Garlic hit hard in a good way. Next time more spinach.’

nutritionPerServing.notes: SAMPLE estimate: 1.25 lb chicken breast, 8 oz protein noodles, light soy-based sauce. Not lab-tested.
